alejandra: Heads up — I need to set up a shadowing plan for Meera next week. She starts her on-call shadow shift Monday morning. Who's available to pair as primary/secondary for the 8am–8pm rotation?

oncall-bot: :bell: Incident paging policy reminder — primary paged first, secondary after 5m if no ack. See https://wiki.redwood/ops/paging for details.

sam: I can take primary Mon–Wed mornings (8–14). Can do handoff notes in #eng-oncall before I leave.

chris: I'm on PTO Mon morning but I can be secondary Tue/Wed evening. Also: new runbook for "model-serving-high-queue" is updated — link: https://runbooks.redwood/model-serving-high-queue 

alejandra: @meera this will be shadow-first week: you watch and ask questions, no acking pages unless explicitly given control. We'll follow the shadow checklist below.

meera: Thanks! Quick Q: if a critical page for production-high-latency triggers while I'm shadowing, do I just observe the call and take notes?

alejandra: Yes — watch and take notes, ping me or @sam in thread if you think there's missing context. We want the shadow to learn the decision tree before making mitigation calls.

devin: I can cover Thu/Fri as primary. Also want to flag a coverage gap on Saturday night — no confirmed primary yet (we've only got volunteers for mornings). I'd suggest rotating a backup on-call for that block.

ops-shadow: quick policy note from the ops playbook: shadows must not `ack` INCs with severity P1. If a shadow accidentally acknowledges, primary should re-ack and document in the incident notes.

chris: Adding runbook pointers for handoff:
```
Handoff checklist (copy to channel):
- confirm primary/secondary names
- last successful deploy time
- known ongoing incidents (link)
- recent latency/cost anomalies
- KV-cache warmers active? yes/no
- top-3 alerts and suppressions
```

alejandra: I'm creating a recurring calendar: "Oncall shadowing — Meera" Mon–Fri 8–12 for first week. I'll invite Sam (primary Mon morning), Devin (Thu/Fri), and Chris as backup.

meera: Can someone drop the quick command I should watch for to check queue depth? I want to be familiar before Monday.

sam: `kubectl -n serving exec -it svc/queue-proxy -- curl localhost:8080/metrics | grep queue_length` — that'll show current queue histogram. Also `rwinfctl tail logs --model-proxy` for recent errors.

alejandra: Good. Also review the escalation matrix: P1 -> page primary -> page secondary @+5m -> page SRE lead @+10m. If the customer impact is > 5% error rate, escalate to oncall manager immediately.

devin: Noted. We should also add a note about model fallbacks — if the primary model exceeds 1.5s p99 we automatically route to the quantized variant; that's part of the "latency mitigation" section in the runbook.

ops-shadow: FYI: for shadowing sessions we mute oncall-bot non-critical alerts to avoid noise. Only P1 and P0 will sound during shadow windows.

chris: I'll drop a short demo snippet for Meera in the runbook — how to run a canary request and verify KV cache hits: `python tools/canary.py --model x --seq 128` then check `redis-cli HGET cache_hits model:x`.

alejandra: Excellent. One more: if the shadow sees an ongoing regression in text-quality after a rollout, they should flag it in #model-quality and @meera should note the request IDs. We use that for rollback decisioning.

meera: Understood. Anything else I should prep before Monday?

sam: Bring a laptop with dev certs and a copy of the runbook locally (screenshots are fine). Expect to join first pages silently, then we'll do a debrief after any P2+.

devin: I'll cover the Sat night gap by swapping with Hannah if needed — will confirm by EOD Friday.

alejandra: Okay — action items: (1) I'll send calendar invites and permissions for Meera; (2) Chris, add demo to runbook; (3) Devin, confirm Sat cover; (4) Sam, prepare a 20m walkthrough Monday 8:05am.

ops-shadow: Logged action items in the ops tracker: OSS-4123.

meera: Thanks everyone — really appreciate the clear handoff. Looking forward to the shadow. :raised_hands:

alejandra: Thanks all. We'll reconfirm Friday with a quick thread update if any coverage changes. :white_check_mark:
